name: V3b: V3a geometry unchanged; the ramjet lightoff gate is what moved
how_to_refly: MEDIUM_MODEL_CD0_FRONTAL=0.1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/Scripts/python scripts/medium_model_v3b_final.py --climb 10 --dive 9.890 --floor 133.14 --lightoff 0.30 --tag v3b   (omit --span/--ar: they default to the frozen wing, and re-typing them rounded is how the 0.376/0.389 confusion started)

propulsion.lightoff_rule: set the gate to the Mach reached at top of climb, approached from above. Top-of-climb altitude is 589 m for every climb angle (it is fixed by dive angle + floor); top-of-climb MACH falls with climb angle: 0.369 at 8 deg, 0.336 at 10 deg, 0.305 at 12 deg, 0.274 at 14 deg (closed-form). At climb 10 deg the 0.30 gate fires at 581 m -- 98.6% of top of climb -- which is the best result measured.
propulsion.note: lightoff_mach is passed explicitly to FpPropulsion; medium_model/constants.py still reads RAMJET_MIN_LIGHTOFF_MACH = 0.45 for the closed-form path. See task #42.

optimizer_results.note: carried over from V3a unchanged -- V3b changes no geometry, so the mass build-up is identical. Consumers derive loaded fuel as wet - dry - margin = 22.68 - 12.57 - 7.42 = 2.69 kg.

gates.powered_accel_0.25g: FAIL (0.049) -- climb-limited, never met in any config
gates.powered_thrust_margin_1.15: FAIL (1.078) -- never met in any config

verified_mission.reproducibility: traverse is +/-0.02 g run-to-run: the FP snapshot store warm-starts each engine solve from prior converged cycles, so the same config reached via a different sequence of flights converges slightly differently (0.376 from the joint sweep, 0.389 standalone).

change: NO GEOMETRY CHANGE. initial_climb_angle_deg 16.657 -> 10.0 and the ramjet lightoff gate 0.45 -> 0.30. Traverse 0.167 -> 0.389 g (2.3x) on the same airframe. The FP engine cannot hold the frozen 16.657 deg climb -- it decelerates into a stall at M 0.118. The lightoff gate is NON-MONOTONE and interacts with climb angle: at climb 8 deg the same 0.30 gate gives 0.052 g because it fires mid-climb. Rule: set the gate to the Mach reached at top of climb.

alternative_not_flight_verified.why_retracted: the +21% thrust was measured at ONE point, M 0.15 / 60 m (launch). Across the flight envelope the duct is DEAD: 0.94 N at M 0.25/300 m, 0.95 at M 0.35/300, 0.96 at M 0.45/300, 1.10 at M 0.54/300, 1.36 at M 0.54/900. It sustains only at launch. t/D 4.00 is below the repo's own >= ~4.5 rule, and that rule was itself derived at M 0.15 -- the sustain boundary MOVES WITH MACH and no launch-condition test can see it.
alternative_not_flight_verified.generalisable_lesson: a pulsejet sustain check at one operating point is not a sustain check; verify alive at top-of-climb AND at the lightoff condition
alternative_not_flight_verified.consolation: 235 mm chamber held at V3a's t/D 4.80 gives +36% FP thrust, but is 188 mm LONGER, not 39 mm shorter

known_issues.stale_dry_mass: design.json dry_mass_kg 12.5696 is STALE: recomputing vehicle_dry_mass from this file's own geometry gives 15.4965 kg (+2.927 kg). Independently confirmed by two agents. Inherited from docs/v3_frozen; affects V3a/V3b/V3c equally since loaded fuel is derived as wet - dry - margin. The 235 mm design built during the V3c campaign recomputes correctly (machine-zero agreement).
